clue.text: Civil servant caught whistle-blower under desk

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming under a piece means being placed after it

parts.note: a bureau is a writing desk with drawers
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
a rat is slang for an informer who tells on others

explanation.surface: An official is nabbed when an informant is found hiding beneath an office desk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' puts C and RAT below BUREAU, so the charade reads BUREAU + C + RAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A government official working in an administrative department is a classic bureaucrat, a synonym for a civil servant.

clue.text: Braved changes daily, weekly or yearly perhaps

indicators.note: the letters of the word braved undergo changes, i.e. are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone bravely faces a routine of change on every timescale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks the definition as examples: words like daily or weekly describe how often something is done.
explanation.definitionFit: Daily, weekly and yearly can all modify verbs to say how often, so they are examples of this part of speech.

clue.text: Starting off chaos and confusion bears fruit

indicators.note: the start of the synonym for chaos is taken off, removing its first letter

parts.note: havoc means widespread chaos
ado means fuss or confusion

explanation.surface: From disorder and muddle, something comes good and bears fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starting off' removes the H from HAVOC, leaving AVOC.
explanation.definitionFit: This pear-shaped green-skinned produce with a large stone is botanically a berry, a kind of fruit.

clue.text: A groom follows feline into vault

indicators.note: the words a groom come after the synonym for feline

parts.note: a cat is a feline
to comb hair is to groom it

explanation.surface: A stable hand trails a cat into a cellar.
explanation.definitionFit: An underground burial chamber with tunnels is a kind of vault for the dead.

clue.text: Short month with German psychiatrist

indicators.note: short means the month's name is cut, losing its last letter

parts.note: June is a month

explanation.surface: A German psychiatrist is on a brief monthly visit.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Jung was the Swiss psychiatrist who founded analytical psychology, so he is an example of the profession.

clue.text: Molluscs initially shelled by Parisian who died

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word shelled

parts.note: qui is French for who, as a Parisian would say it
D is the usual abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: Shellfish were shelled by a Frenchman who then died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Molluscs' looks like it gives an initial letter, but it is the definition; 'initially' works on 'shelled'.
explanation.definitionFit: Squid are cephalopods, a class of soft-bodied sea creatures within the mollusc group.

clue.text: First class fashions coming from South Island

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming from the south means the letters read upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: A1 means first class, written A and I
cults are crazes or fashions

explanation.surface: Top-quality fashions arrive from a southern island.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is read with the 1 as the letter I; reading AICULTS upwards gives the island.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Lucia is a Caribbean island nation in the Windward Islands.

clue.text: Way to cross by tube

parts.note: via means by way of
a duct is a tube or channel

explanation.surface: A route over somewhere, travelling by Underground train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tube' suggests the London Underground, but it is just a pipe here.
explanation.definitionFit: A long bridge carrying a road or railway over a valley is a means of crossing it.

clue.text: Buff spot on Edwardian screens

indicators.note: the phrase spot on Edwardian screens, i.e. conceals, the letters within it

explanation.surface: A film enthusiast is spot on about Edwardian screen shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buff' reads as an enthusiast, but here it means fit and muscular.
explanation.definitionFit: Buff is slang for physically fit with visible muscle, as is a toned body.

clue.text: Run away when left in charge

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for left inside the word for charge

parts.note: a fee is a charge

explanation.surface: Someone bolts when left in charge of something.
explanation.definitionFit: To flee is to escape or bolt, a direct synonym of running away.

clue.text: Old flame putting on new outfit for swapping

parts.note: an ex is a former partner, an old flame
changing is putting on different clothes

explanation.surface: A former lover is getting dressed in something new.
explanation.definitionFit: Trading one thing for another is swapping, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Cursed roughly about books being abandoned

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the abbreviation for books
roughly signals the letters of cursed are rearranged

parts.note: B is an abbreviation for book, so BB is books

explanation.surface: Someone swore crudely about books that had been left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' is the definition in its informal sense of cancelled, as a scrubbed mission.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan that is scrubbed has been cancelled or dropped, the informal sense of abandoned.

clue.text: Germany, overwhelmed by seven balls, go too far

indicators.note: overwhelmed by puts the abbreviation for Germany inside the letters for seven balls

parts.note: a cricket over is six balls, and one more ball is O, so seven balls is OVER plus O
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: Germany is swamped in a game, and someone overdoes it.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six deliveries; adding a ball-shaped O makes seven.
explanation.definitionFit: To overdo something is to take it to excess, an idiomatic equivalent of going too far.

clue.text: Conductors choose right verses

parts.note: to elect is to choose
odes are poems, i.e. verses

explanation.surface: Orchestra conductors select the correct verses to perform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conductors' suggests orchestra leaders, but here it means things that carry electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: These terminals pass electric current into or out of a medium, so they are electrical conductors.

clue.text: Far right try to cover up a complete mess

indicators.note: to cover up means the other pieces surround and hide the letter a

parts.note: to have a go is to try

explanation.surface: Extreme right-wingers attempt a cover-up of a total shambles.
explanation.definitionFit: A farrago is a confused jumble or hotchpotch, i.e. a complete mess.

clue.text: Menagerie in Denmark engulfed by fumes — crikey!

indicators.note: engulfed by means the inner letters are swallowed inside the word for fumes

parts.note: gas is fumes

indicators.note: in places the menagerie's letters inside Denmark's abbreviation

parts.note: DK is the abbreviation and vehicle code for Denmark
a zoo is a menagerie, a collection of animals

explanation.surface: A Danish zoo is filled with fumes, prompting an exclamation of shock.
explanation.definitionFit: This old-fashioned exclamation of surprise is a mild oath, just like crikey.

clue.text: Stuff bringing protests

definitions.meaning: stuff as a noun means things or items
protests as a verb means raises disapproval

explanation.surface: Material that provokes objections.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both things in general and the verb for complaining against something.

clue.text: Oddly, tear not unusual in childish fit

indicators.note: oddly picks the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of the words tear not

parts.note: rum is old slang for odd or unusual

explanation.surface: A rare tear appears in a child's outburst.
explanation.definitionFit: A tantrum is an outburst of temper typical of a small child, a childish fit.

clue.text: Fruit variety in outsize container

indicators.note: in places the word for variety inside the abbreviation for outsize

parts.note: OS is the clothing-size abbreviation for outsize
a range is a variety or assortment

explanation.surface: Assorted fruit packed in a huge box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'container' is only a link word here, not a containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Citrus fruits of a familiar bright colour are one example of fruit.

clue.text: Drunk, wet, sad, devastated

indicators.note: devastated means wrecked, so the letters of wet and sad are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A sorry drunk: soaked, miserable and crushed.
explanation.definitionFit: Wasted is slang for very intoxicated, a synonym of drunk.

clue.text: Sailor heads North following a selection of maps

indicators.note: following places the reversed sailor after the letter a
in a down clue, heading north means the letters run upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: a salt, as in old salt, is a seasoned sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor sets off northwards guided by a set of charts.
explanation.definitionFit: An atlas is a bound collection of maps, a selection of them in book form.

clue.text: Engineer into a plastic, tubular dish

parts.note: to rig is to engineer or fix an outcome

indicators.note: plastic means malleable, so the letters of into a are remoulded

explanation.surface: An engineer gets into a plastic pipe-shaped vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: This ridged pasta comes in short tubes, so a plate of it is a tubular dish.

clue.text: Good recipe, simple to follow and oily

indicators.note: to follow places the word for simple after the first two letters

parts.note: R is an abbreviation for recipe, from the Latin on prescriptions
easy means simple

explanation.surface: A tasty recipe that is easy to follow and rather oily.
explanation.definitionFit: Something greasy is covered in or full of fat, much the same as oily.

clue.text: Capacity of graceful cat

parts.note: fluid movement is smooth and graceful
the ounce is another name for the snow leopard

explanation.surface: How much a lithe cat can hold.
explanation.definitionFit: This unit of liquid volume is a measure of capacity in imperial and US systems.

clue.text: Holly sees priest returning to cross

indicators.note: returning means the priest's name is read backwards

parts.note: Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel, a crossword favourite
X is a cross

explanation.surface: Holly goes to see a priest as he comes back to the cross.
explanation.definitionFit: Ilex is the botanical genus to which holly belongs, also used for the holm oak.

clue.text: Farmer goes around exhibiting beast

indicators.note: around signals that the concealed letters are turned round to read backwards
the words Farmer goes are exhibiting, i.e. displaying, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A farmer walks about, showing off a prize animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-eating giant of folklore is a monstrous brute, a beast.

clue.text: A little spot of sun to lightly kiss the French

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for sun, as on calendars for Sunday
a peck is a light, quick kiss
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A bit of sunshine for giving the French a quick kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: A speckle is a small dot or fleck of colour, a little spot.

clue.text: Cook special meal with a dash of marmite

parts.note: tea is a light evening meal in British usage

indicators.note: a dash of takes just the first letter of the word marmite

explanation.surface: Preparing a special supper spiced up with a little Marmite.
explanation.walkthrough: Marmite is a British savoury yeast spread; in Britain 'tea' can mean the evening meal.
explanation.definitionFit: To steam food is one way to cook it, so this is an example of cooking.
